title: Ryt.Life
about: Ryt.Life is a mental healthcare platform connecting patients with providers — video consultations, appointment booking, and prescription reminders, designed with anonymity and confidentiality as first-class constraints given the sensitivity of the subject. I worked on the UI/UX across the patient, doctor, and admin-facing sides of the product.

process.title: Booking care needed to feel safe
process.text: Mental healthcare carries real stigma — booking an appointment, joining a video call, and messaging a doctor all needed to feel private and low-friction, for patients who might already be uneasy about seeking care.

process.title: Mapping every user's flow separately
process.text: I flow-charted the product across its three distinct users — patients booking and rescheduling appointments, doctors managing their own schedules, and admins handling escalations — building in anonymity and confidentiality controls, prescription reminders, and an FAQ layer to reduce hesitation before booking.

process.title: A reference for engineering handoff
process.text: The flows and UI became the reference for engineering handoff across video consultation, scheduling, and the doctor-facing admin tools.
